answer: Histories are stored in ivory, checked in velvet, and prism reveals each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 1 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases as the record follows the key, which means laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 4366 identities would post 2011 proofs and burn roughly 8 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
